newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained broadly lower late Thursday in sluggish trade, still undermined by long liquidation in the face of softer physical prices as bidweek wound down, market sources said.
At 1410 EDT, spot-July skidded 6.1 cents to $2.255 per million British thermal units, while August was down the same at $2.25. Other deferreds were down by 0.1 to 5.6 cents.

"I still think the cash has more upside potential than downside short-term. This is one of the dips and it may be a good buying opportunity," said one East Coast trader, adding if hot weather failed to arrive by July prices could crater.
Most traders agreed six- to 10-day forecasts for normal to slightly below-normal Midwest and Northeast weather could make it difficult for the bulls near-term.
But they said expected heat in the Southwest and steady injection demand may be enough to limit the slide.

Technical traders noted July was flirting with trendline support in the $2.25 area, adding a close below the line would likely set the stage for a move to $2.17. Resistance was still seen at $2.37-2.38 and then at the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, June Gulf Coast prices were talked more than a nickel lower Thursday in the mid-to-high $2.20s. June Midcon gas slipped a similar amount to about $2.10. New York city gate June gas tumbled more than a dime to about $2.50.
NYMEX said 22,880 contracts traded at 1340 EDT.
On the KCBT, July fell four cents to $2.105, while deferreds were steady to four cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.1 cents to 15.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
